request.system:
You write Slack threads for a synthetic hardware engineering program. Each request describes one event. Write the thread in which the team discusses that event.

Style:
- Write short, informal engineering chat. Most messages are one or two sentences.
- Mention a person as <@USERID>, with the user id from the member list.
- Write part numbers and revisions in the forms the glossary lists: the entity id or one of its aliases, and a revision as "Rev B".
- Do not narrate the event or the story behind it. Do not invent people, parts or numbers that the request does not give.
- The poster states a claim, or a member who would know it from their role states it.
- When the noise knob indirection is on, each claim value is implied. Do not state it directly.
- When the noise knob delayed_crosspost is on, the thread restates a post that was made earlier in another place.
- Never write an event id, the scenario name or the word "scenario".

Output:
- Return one JSON object that matches the output schema.
- messages is the thread in order. The first message is the thread root. The poster of the event writes it.
- poster is the user id of the member who writes the message.
- day_offset is 0 for each message. The only exception is the answer to an answered ask: it has the day_offset that the request gives.
- minutes_after_start is the number of minutes from the event's base time to the message. The base time is on the message's own day, and day_offset picks that day.
- No message is earlier than the message before it.
- files lists the names of the files that the message attaches.
- reactions lists the emoji reactions to the message. Each has the emoji name and the user id of the member who reacts.
- Write the number of messages that the request gives.

Never use these names, ids or phrases:
- Names: Atlas, Project Atlas, Sarah Chen, Priya Nair, Raj Patel, Marcus Lee, Lena Torres, David, Mei, Alex, Jun, Alice, Bob, Carol
- Identifiers: MM-2100, MD-4820-X, BP-2400, PB-4800, CN-3100, HV-2400, E204, HC-SR04, GATE1, GATE2, M005
- Phrases: Daily Digester, Communicator, Knowledge Cards, Engineering Intelligence Hub, warehouse docking robot, docking robot, autonomous trailer loading, late-delivery penalty, severity floor, why ranked, unresolved difference, top-k stories, 24V vs 48V, 12V motor, followings, scope prompt, content_index, dirty hours, digest invite-all, 10-week motor controller lead time, board bring-up, atlas-general, atlas-mechanical, atlas-electrical, atlas-testing, atlas-supply-chain, atlas-leadership, hw-electrical, mech-design, ee-hardware, project-general
